claim: The docs index lists 804 pages: 368 ElevenAgents, 404 API reference, 432 help-center, 40 Reception.ai, 66 ElevenAPI, 43 overview; we saved 258 agents/Reception.ai/overview pages as Markdown.

ElevenAgents surfaces documented: builder (prompt, workflows graph, free-form and structured procedures, knowledge base/RAG, tools: client, webhook, code, MCP, system tools), voice (multi-voice, pronunciation dictionaries, expressive mode, audio environment), channels (widget, web/mobile SDKs, WhatsApp, SMS, Slack, Telegram, Teams, custom channel), telephony (Twilio native, Exotel native, SIP trunk, Vonage, CCaaS: Genesys, Five9, Amazon Connect), operate (versioning with branches/merge proposals, environments, experiments, agent testing and simulation, analytics, Spotlight, real-time monitoring, alerts, triage tickets, OpenTelemetry traces, CLI, hosted MCP), privacy (retention, audio saving, redaction, Zero Retention Mode) and legal pages (HIPAA, TCPA, disclosure).

ElevenAgents Architect is an in-product LLM assistant that investigates conversations, edits an agent on a branch, writes and runs tests, and opens a merge proposal; it cannot review/merge, has no scheduled or background work yet, and acts as the user.

Reception.ai is a separate SMB product on the same docs site: AI receptionist with scheduling (services, staff, locations, booking page), a client list, orders, quote requests, SMS notifications and its own plans; US/Canada numbers, other countries via a regulatory request.

Outbound at scale in the public product is Batch Calling: upload CSV/XLS with a mandatory phone_number column (other columns become dynamic variables; language/first_message/system_prompt/voice_id columns override the agent), send now or at one scheduled time in a timezone, test-call one recipient, monitor per-recipient status. Concurrency defaults to min(50% of workspace, 70% of agent) limits; Zero Retention Mode cannot be used with batch calls.

The signed-out dashboard bundle carries a generated API client for an unpublished outbound-campaigns product: campaigns submit/pause/resume/stop/progress/calls/export, campaign leads with a suppressLead mutation, an attention queue (resolve/retry), workspace campaign config and a pre-revoke-status check. None of these 23 routes is in the public OpenAPI or docs. Conversation records already carry campaign_id, campaign_lead_id, cold_attempt and conversation_type (initial/retry/callback/redirect).

Inference from EL-06: ElevenLabs is building a lead-level campaign control plane (retries, callbacks, suppression, an exceptions queue) on top of batch calling; the 2026-10-17 parity row "no campaign control plane comparable to Vapi/Bolna" is true of the public product today but is likely to expire.

The dashboard bundle also references unpublished automations (with schedule-preview and runs), task-agents/task-runs, company-oracle (knowledge sources with ingest), templates (browse, from-agent), cloud-storage-destinations and analytics queries (latency, LLM cost, interruptions, concurrency and queue over time): 326 convai routes in the bundle are absent from the public OpenAPI.

The public OpenAPI (api.elevenlabs.io/openapi.json, 2.3 MB) has 322 paths and 1,644 schemas; 141 paths are /v1/convai (214 operations incl. speech-engine and flows). Groups: agents 34, knowledge-base 25, conversations 15, MCP servers 8, agent-testing 7, batch-calling 6, triage-tickets 5, phone-numbers 3.

There is no contacts/leads/CRM object in the public API; the end-user object is a user_id string passed at conversation start, listed by GET /v1/convai/users (exact-match search). Campaign-like state lives only in batch calls (status pending/in_progress/completed/failed/cancelled; recipient status adds dispatched/initiated/voicemail) with a single retry endpoint.

Phone numbers are import-only (POST /v1/convai/phone-numbers accepts Twilio, Exotel or SIP-trunk credentials); ElevenLabs does not sell numbers to ElevenAgents customers. TelephonyProvider enum = twilio, sip_trunk, exotel.

Each conversation record exposes termination_reason, error {code, reason}, call_result (answered/voicemail/busy/no_answer/failed), per-call SIP messages, queue_wait_secs, main_language, feature usage flags, per-call cost and cost_fiat (USD), LLM/TTS/ASR usage, and an OpenTelemetry trace format. Conversations can be filtered by 40 parameters incl. termination_reasons, tool errors, evaluation and data-collection values, topics and guardrail triggers.

Agent config defaults in the schema: LLM gemini-2.5-flash, TTS eleven_v4_turbo, ASR provider scribe_realtime (changed from elevenlabs on 2026-06-08), turn model turn_v3, turn_eagerness normal, turn_timeout 7 s, soft-timeout filler default text "Hhmmmm...yeah." (off by default), speculative_turn off.

The LLM enum has 111 values: OpenAI GPT-4o..GPT-6.1, Google Gemini 1.5..4 Argon, Anthropic Claude 3..Opus 5.5, xAI Grok, and ElevenLabs-hosted open models (Qwen3/3.5/3.6, GLM 4.5-Air/5.2, DeepSeek Flash 4.1, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4, Watt-tool 8B/70B); custom LLM via chat_completions, responses or websocket APIs; backup-LLM cascade on by default.

Two first-party speech-to-speech Realtime models (eleven_realtime_v1_mini default, v1_max) are rolling out by workspace; Max is not available in India or Singapore residency; an OpenAI-Realtime-compatible endpoint exists.

Voice sessions from the official client SDK (@elevenlabs/client 1.29.0) default to WebRTC via livekit-client ^2.21.0 against wss://livekit.rtc.elevenlabs.io (EU and India residency have their own livekit.rtc.<region>.residency hosts); text-only, signed-URL and orchestrator sessions use WebSocket wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/conversation. React Native needs @livekit/react-native.

The data model names LiveKit throughout: authorization methods livekit_token/livekit_token_website, features_usage.is_livekit, a LivekitStackType (standard/static) on SIP numbers, and "Whether a LiveKit SIP outbound trunk is configured" on SIP config.

Inference from EL-16/17 + DNS: ElevenLabs runs its own LiveKit (server and LiveKit SIP) under its own domains on Google Cloud rather than LiveKit Cloud, Pipecat or Vocode; orchestration (turn model, ASR, TTS, LLM routing) is its own.

Every HTTP/WebSocket/LiveKit hostname we resolved (api, api.us, elevenlabs.io, livekit.rtc, and the eu/in/sg residency equivalents) sits in Google Cloud prefixes with scope "global" (global external load balancer anycast), so their backend region is not visible from DNS.

SIP is regional and visible: sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io resolves to 136.112.48.140 in GCP us-central1; sip.rtc.in.residency.elevenlabs.io to 34.100.197.221 in asia-south1 (Mumbai); EU to europe-west1; SG to asia-southeast1. Static-IP SIP hosts (sip-static.rtc.*) sit in 199.88.252.0/24, which ARIN registers to Eleven Labs Inc; the docs say that /24 spans US, EU, India and Singapore.

Inference from EL-20: a standard (non-Enterprise) Indian customer on SIP has media anchored in Iowa, adding roughly one India-US round trip (~200-250 ms; Azure Central India-East US is 201 ms) to every turn, and is exposed to the TRAI rule that Indian SIP termination needs an Indian server (Plivo states this for Vapi). India residency (Enterprise only) moves SIP to Mumbai.

One 25 s public demo call on elevenlabs.io/conversational-ai (synthetic caller clip, 2026-10-20 17:56 UTC) used a WebSocket to wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/conversation from react_sdk 0.14.0-beta.0 (not WebRTC), agent output pcm_44100, user input pcm_16000, server ping 216-223 ms from our US-East egress; 113 frames received (95 audio, 16 ping), 282 sent (262 user_audio_chunk). The demo agent sends no AI disclosure in its first message ("Hey, how can I help you today?").

Speech stack is first-party: ASR Scribe v2 Realtime (scribe_realtime; scribe_v2_turbo also in enum), TTS Eleven v4 Turbo default (also v4, v3 conversational, flash/turbo v2.5, multilingual v2), own turn-detection model turn_v3, own RAG embeddings (e5_mistral_7b_instruct, multilingual_e5_large_instruct). Only the LLM is third-party by default.

Gemini and Claude agent LLM prices are "aligned with Vertex AI regional pricing ... a 10% increase", and LLM availability is filtered by data residency, so these models are inferred to be called through Google Vertex AI regional endpoints.

Platform plumbing seen on the signed-out app page: Next.js (Turbopack chunks under elevenlabs.io/app_assets), MobX, Google Identity Toolkit (Firebase Auth) for sign-in, Stripe, hCaptcha, PostHog proxied via /dachshund, VWO, Clarity, Sentry, and a Cloud Function us-central1-xi-labs.cloudfunctions.net/geolocation (GCP project xi-labs).
The convai widget core (0.21.0) bundles @fingerprintjs/fingerprintjs 5.x and Preact; the widget fingerprints the browser (inferred use: abuse limiting or anonymous user identity).

Job posts (157 open, 2026-10-20): Infrastructure Engineer asks for Kubernetes at scale, strong GCP, GPU clusters for training and inference "across cloud and on-prem"; Research Engineer - Inference names CUDA, Triton, TensorRT, vLLM, SGLang. No job post mentions LiveKit, SIP or WebRTC. India roles: AE Mid-Market, Account Manager, Deployment Strategist Lead (Bangalore preferred), EA India & ME.

Private deployment ("enclave") mode exists: the client SDK builds an enclave_setup_config with agent config, tools, knowledge base, an optional AWS Bedrock inference profile and post-call webhooks; docs list private deployments of ElevenAgents, TTS and STT inside the customer cloud.

ElevenAgents list price 2026-10-20: $0.08 per call minute on every plan (Free 15 min/4 concurrent; Starter $6 75/6; Creator $22 275/10; Pro $99 1,238/20; Scale $299 3,738/30; Business $990 12,375/40), burst above the concurrency limit at $0.16 (up to 3x concurrency), text messages $0.003, LLM billed on top at provider rates, no ElevenLabs telephony fee. Unchanged in USD from 2026-06-06 and 2026-10-17 (l4a pricing-history.json).
Silent periods are billed at 5% of the per-minute rate; queue wait time is not billed.

All-in list price for an Indian outbound minute at FX 95: INR 8.17-8.92 via Exotel or Plivo (platform INR 7.60 + LLM INR 0.19-0.72 + telephony INR 0.38-0.60); INR 15.8-16.5 in burst; INR 12.5-15.0 via Twilio to an Indian mobile. That is about 2x Sarvam (INR 3.4-3.9) and above the INR 3.5-7 Indian band.
The $0.08 platform fee is 3.9x what the same ASR and TTS cost on ElevenLabs' own API list (Scribe v2 Realtime $0.39/h = $0.0065/min plus Flash/Turbo TTS $0.04 per 1K chars x 352 chars = $0.0141/min).

Reconstructed platform COGS (own ASR + own TTS on own GPUs, self-hosted LiveKit on GCP, LLM passed through): INR 0.20-1.38 per minute, implying 82-97% gross margin on the INR 7.60 platform fee; ElevenLabs could price an Indian minute near Sarvam's and stay profitable.
India billing: subscriptions can be paid in INR with UPI for customers located in India; prices are otherwise identical.

32 changelog entries from 2026-04-01 to 2026-10-12 (about weekly) carry 296 headline items, 195 of them in the ElevenAgents section (median 6 per entry), plus API diffs and SDK releases each week. Notable dated launches: Exotel native telephony 2026-06-01, memory tool types 2026-06-15, backchannel detection 2026-07-13, batch export 2026-07-27, concurrency wait queues 2026-08-17, triage tickets 2026-08-24, batch campaign context 2026-08-31, Twilio AMD 2026-09-07, alerting 2026-09-21, merge proposals 2026-10-05.

SDK cadence: elevenlabs-js and elevenlabs-python v2.72.0 in the 2026-10-12 changelog; npm/PyPI already at 2.74.0/2.74.1 on 2026-10-20; @elevenlabs/client 1.29.0, react 1.19.0, convai-widget-core 0.21.0.

Public status page (incident.io; RSS covers 2026-07-31..2026-10-13): 25 incidents in 75 days; 9 name Agents, SIP, Twilio, batch calling or conversation history; 4 are SIP/Twilio telephony; 5 are EU-residency. Components include Conversations, Telephony ("Native Telephony: SIP + Twilio"), RAG, Quality ("Slower turns, increased latency") and UI.

Exotel is a first-class provider since 2026-06-01: Exotel Voicebot applet streams 8 kHz PCM over WebSocket to wss://api(.in.residency).elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/conversation/exotel; outbound uses Exotel Calls/connect with the customer's API key/token; Mumbai (api.in.exotel.com) and Singapore clusters; Voicebot applet is gated and needs Exotel support (1-2 business days); transfers need a chained Connect applet.

India data residency exists as an Enterprise-only isolated environment (in.residency.elevenlabs.io, separate workspace and API key); storage is in India but "processing may nevertheless occur outside", Realtime v1 Max is unavailable there, and agents must be recreated (no migration). This corrects the 2026-10-17 parity row "Data residency page (EU/US); no India region found".

Across 258 saved agents/overview docs pages there is no mention of TRAI, DLT, NCPR/DND, 140/160-series or Indian calling hours; the only telemarketing-law page is TCPA (US). Batch calling has no calling-window, DNC or consent field; the TCPA page tells the buyer to keep DNC lists, honour 8am-9pm and record consent. India compliance is left to the buyer (confirms ledger CMP-27).

AI disclosure and recording consent are a contractual duty of the buyer (ElevenAgents terms): notice must precede any interaction; the sample verbal line is "Hi, I'm an AI assistant. This call may be recorded...". The platform does not inject it.

The India marketing page claims voices "tuned for Indian accents and code-switched speech", 12 Indian languages and accents in the voice library, Hinglish tuning, Ozonetel/Exotel/Plivo integrations, forward-deployed engineering, India residency, SOC 2 Type II/ISO 27001/PCI DSS L1, and Indian agent customers Meesho, Cars24 and TVS Motor. No benchmark is published; "Hinglish" appears nowhere in the docs.

Twilio regional routing supports only us1/ie1/au1 region IDs in the API; Twilio numbers default to us1 even for non-US numbers. An Indian buyer on Twilio is therefore routed through the US (Twilio also allows outbound to India only from non-Indian numbers, per the vapi lane).

ASR and TTS language lists include Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu and Assamese; language switching mid-call needs the language-detection system tool, which is off by default and is triggered by the LLM.

Measured on 2026-10-17 (l4b, homepage demo, US vantage): clean-turn p50 3.75 s (n=63), end-of-turn transcript p50 2.65 s (n=72), Hindi callers answered in English, "hmm"/"haan" answered with "Are you still there?" on 4/16 short turns, barge-in handled 3/7, a babble session slowed to 8 s and dropped. These are the strongest failure observations available without an account.

Trustpilot: TrustScore 3.0 from 1,192 reviews. Agent-relevant complaints (filtered "agent", WebFetch summary): support unreachable or AI-only ("routes to an AI agent that cannot resolve billing matters and does not transfer to a person", 2026-06-11; "customer support? Non-existent", 2025-12-01), docs ("confusing docs", "brute force an agent at the dashboard and API to figure it out", 2026-10-06), dropped calls without memory ("the call unexpectedly drops out ... answers with no record of the previous conversation", 2026-06-17), WhatsApp integration failing with unanswered tickets (2026-01-12), credits charged for agent mistakes (2026-07-24).

GitHub elevenlabs/packages: 232 issues; the most-discussed are SDK connection/state bugs (#635 agent connects but does not speak, #152 "could not establish pc connection", #257 first WebSocket connection often fails, #143 conversation stays active after endSession, #336 agent stuck in listening mode, #47 request for silence_duration_ms control).

Retell community threads (in l4a complaints.csv) about ElevenLabs as a TTS inside Retell: v3 stutter, sentences skipped, v3 billing by generated speech vs call duration, cost of ElevenLabs TTS; 12 of 869 coded items.

HN (Algolia, 211 comments since 2025-10): few agent complaints; one says "Elevenlabs using a completely incapable voice agent for sales outreach made me wonder if they were actively trying to dissuade customers" (2026-05-10, item 48088509); one on billing lock-in to a Google account (2026-04-05, item 47653609). An ElevenLabs employee says they chose a cascading model "because it's better suited for enterprise use cases" (2025-12-11, item 46236377).

Complaint code profile for ElevenAgents from accessible sources: SUPPORT and DOCS/UX dominate review text; RELIABILITY shows in SDK issues and 9 agent/telephony incidents in 75 days; CONVERSATION (latency, language hold, backchannels) shows only in our own measurements. Reddit, G2 and the GitHub API were blocked (403) and were not bypassed, so this profile is thin.

Memory across calls is not documented publicly, but the data model has memory entries (MemoryEntrySearchResult with version and a source of conversation or manual; LoadableMemoryEntry; resource type convai_memory_entries) and the dashboard bundle calls /v1/convai/agents/{id}/memories CRUD and /agents/{id}/user-memory/preview. Memory is in development or private beta (inference).

Personalisation today is per-call: dynamic variables, per-conversation overrides (prompt, first message, language, voice), user_id for grouping conversations, and Twilio inbound personalisation webhooks; nothing carries facts from one call to the next without the buyer's own store (the docs recommend summarising history from post-call webhooks).

The optimisation loop is human-gated: Spotlight finds patterns, Architect proposes a branch with tests, a teammate approves the merge proposal, and experiments split traffic deterministically by conversation id and the user promotes the winner by hand (no significance test is documented). "Proactive proposals" and scheduled automations are announced as coming; the bundle already calls /convai/automations and /triage-tickets/{id}/architect-dispatches.

Marketing vs docs: the India page claims Hinglish-tuned speech and India-ready compliance; the docs have no Hinglish guidance and no Indian regulatory controls; the 2026-10-17 demo answered Hindi callers in English. Same pattern as ledger CMP-01 (marketing ahead of docs).

REA 6.7.0: inspect-web-network-capture rejected our Playwright HAR on strict URI format (an unescaped URL at entry 75) and accepted it after percent-encoding, returning a lossless record set (346 records) with no stack inference; analyze-javascript-application on four client-SDK files finished in 6 s and found the fetch/WebSocket call sites but left the host literals unresolved. All stack facts here came from our own SDK, DNS and HAR reading.

Not done by design: no sign-up, no WebRTC token fetch for the public agent (would start a second session), no "Phone call" demo (needs our number), no Reddit/G2 (403, not bypassed). Demo attempts 1-3 clicked the wrong control and started no session; attempt 4 is the one call.
